claim: The Abvigen AFR-0500-COOH product is supplied as a suspension at a mass concentration of 10 mg/ml, in volumes of 10 ml or 20 ml.
validity_conditions: AS SUPPLIED, IN THE BOTTLE. This is the stock, not what is under the objective: any dilution the operator makes stands between this number and the sample, and no dilution is recorded anywhere here. So a caller asking for tracer_number_density in its own sample is not answered by this entry even once the diameter is known -- it is answered by this entry times a dilution factor that is a separate, unrecorded fact. The vendor's Particles/ml table is headed 'For 10 mg/ml', which is this number, and that heading is the only reason the /ml column means anything. 015 WAS WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY IT WAS ISSUED, AND THIS ENTRY IS ABOUT THE TYPE. For a few hours this entry read that the product identification had been withdrawn and that it was not about the bottle on this bench. The person reversed that on 2026-09-19 after the prior project's records were opened: the bottle IS AFR-0500-COOH, and what is wrong is Abvigen's published data. WHAT DECIDED IT WAS AN ASYMMETRY, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and that is worth keeping because the measurement alone did not settle it. Both explanations -- wrong bottle, or wrong data sheet -- predict green-excited particles visible at 605, and 015's own evidence, a label that says nothing, is equally consistent with either. What broke the tie is that the Abvigen page has two documented errors unrelated to any of this (a monoclonal-antibody filing, and the product name printed in the Particle Size field), so `the data sheet is wrong` is far the cheaper explanation. See abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable. AND THE ENTRY IS STILL NOT DIRECTLY ABOUT THE BOTTLE. Under the instance/type split architecture ruled in 6eaee1b, this is a fact about the TYPE `AFR-0500-COOH`, at E3, from the supplier. The bottle is an INSTANCE and lives in the sample table. The claim joining them -- `this bottle is that product` -- carries its own grade and is E5, because the label is still silent and the person's judgement is what stands in for it; it becomes E3 the day somebody reads a label that says. So applying anything here to the particles on the bench inherits E5 by 5.8, worst in the chain. Restored, but not restored to E3. THE `abvigen_` HANDLES STAY, and they are now right for a different reason than the one they were changed for. They were renamed from `tracer_` because the word `tracer` asserted these were ours in a string nothing checks; they keep the name because these are type-level facts and the type is what they should be named for. A query for our tracer should not land here. THE CLAIM SENTENCE WAS CORRECTED TOO, AND IT HAD BEEN THE LAST PLACE THE OLD ASSERTION SURVIVED. The handles were renamed to `abvigen_` hours earlier, and the first words of the claim still read `The tracer particles...` -- so this entry's body said `a query for our tracer should not land here` while its own headline sentence said these were our tracers. Found by librarian-agent-a5 verifying my report against the tree, which is exactly why that verification was handed over: my account came from memory of what I had done. The entry_id still begins `tracer_` and stays that way deliberately -- it is the citation handle, the polystyrene dispersion entries reference it by name, and renaming it is a deletion under rule 8.

identifiers.applies_to: the type AFR-0500-COOH. Applying it to the bottle on this bench goes through the E5 linking claim in the sample table
